combo_label: At the Dentist × Silly English Things × Enid Blyton

entries.clue: Round-cheeked fellow whose slippery-slip spirals down Blyton's tall tree
Competitive pulling of the ugliest possible face, framed by a horse collar
Surname of Blyton's first husband, borrowed for the pen name she once used
Cheap, rough wine bought by the box and drunk without ceremony
Drawn-out treatment that clears a dying nerve from deep inside and seals the space
Hardened deposit on teeth that brushing cannot shift, also a branch of maths
Electric doorstep delivery vehicle that whirrs down the street before dawn
Scrap of old cloth; Blyton's big, bad playroom doll Amelia is made of it
Tiny six-legged marchers that arrive in one long black column
Folded square of open mesh, clamped between the teeth for ten minutes
Wide, soft, flour-dusted morning roll, never sweetened
Eldest and bossiest of the four children in Blyton's most famous band
Eject saliva from the mouth, the one job the patient is given
